EGPE is a cell line obtained from bovine E. granulosus pe G1 maintained at our laboratory. Cells used for experiments were from passages 35 to 40. The cell supernatants were obtained after five-days of cell colony incubation. Cell debris was removed by centrifuging the supernatants three times (3000 rpm). Then, samples were stored in aliquots at -20°C until use. protein fractions obtained after MW cell extract separation by Sephacryl elution were identified by absorbance in a spectrophotometer (Biowave II+ , Biochrome Ltd., Cambridge, England).  by absorbance (205-280 nm). Every fraction with higher absorbance was concentrated through a 3K cut‐off membrane concentrator (Pierce, Thermo Scientific). Protein fraction and EGPE supernantant reactivity was analyzed by Western blot and using a pool of sera from 11 patients with CE with only hepatic localization. The reactive protein fractions were passed through an affinity column (Protein G HP SpinTrap - GE Healthcare) for samples and controls (sera from two patients with cysticercosis and two patients with fascioliasis). Eluted proteins were concentrated through a 3K cut‐off membrane concentrator (Pierce, Thermo Scientific) and, a 15% SDS–PAGE was performed to concentrate and clean-up protein extracts prior to in-gel digestion (data not shown). Obtained bands from Coomassie blue-stained SDS-PAGE were excised, detained, washed, reduced, alkylated and then in-gel digested with 100 ng Trypsin (Promega V5111). Peptides were recovered by elution with 50% acetonitrile- 0.5% trifluoroacetic acid, including brief sonication, and further concentrated by speed – vacuum drying. Samples were resuspended in 15 μL of water containing 0.1% formic acid, desalted using C18zip tips (Merck-millipore) , and eluted in 10 µl of H 2 O:ACN:FA (40:60:01%). The digests were analyzed by nanoLC-MS/MS in a Thermo Scientific QExactive Mass Spectrometer coupled to a nanoHPLC EASY-nLC 1000 (Thermo Scientific). For LC-MS/MS analysis, approximately two μg of peptides were loaded onto the column and eluted for 120 min using a reverse-phase column (C18, 2 µm, 100A, 50 µm x 150 mm) Easy- Spray Column PepMap RSLC (P/N ES801) suitable for separating protein complexes with a high degree of resolution. The flow rate used for the nanocolumn was 300 nL 1000-1 and the solvent range from 7% B (5 min) to 35%. The gradient duration was 120 min. Solvent A was 0.1% formic acid in water, whereas B was 0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile.. The injection volume was 2µL. The MS equipment has a high collision dissociation cell (HCS) for fragmentation and an Orbitrap analyzer (Thermoscientific, Q-Exacted). A voltage of 3.5 kV was used for Electro Spray Ionization (Thermo Scientific, EASY-SPRAY). XCalibur 3.0.63 (Thermo Scientific) software was used for data acquisition. Full-scan mass spectra was acquired in an Orbitrap analyzer. The scanned mass range was 400-1800 m/z, at a resolution of 70,000 at 400 m/z, and the twelve most intense ions in each cycle were sequentially isolated, fragmented by higher- energy collision dissociation, and measured in an Orbitrap analyzer. Peptides with a charge of +1 or with an unassigned charge state were excluded from fragmentation for MS2.
dataProcessingProtocol: QExactive raw data was processed using the Proteome Discoverer software (version 2.1.1.21, Thermo Scientific) and searched against the E. granulosus sequences database UniProt  with trypsin specificity and a maximum of one missed cleavage per peptide. Carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues was set as a fixed modification and oxidation of methionine was set as variable modification. Proteome Discoverer searches were performed with a precursor mass tolerance of 10 ppm and product ion tolerance of 0.05 Da. Protein hits were filtered for at least one high- confidence peptide matched with a maximum protein and peptide false discovery rate of 1%, calculated by using a reverse database strategy

sampleProcessingProtocol: The cell wall proteome of C. auris CECT13225 was obtained following the method published by Pitartch and coworkers (2002). Briefly C. auris was grown at 37 °C and 120 rpms O/N. The obtained pellet was then washed five times with ice-cold lysis buffer (10 mM tris-HCL, pH 7.4 and 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF)). Cells were resuspended in the same buffer and added to eppendorfs containing the same volume of crystal beads (0.5 mm diameter) and disrupted at 28 Hz for 20 min using the Millmix 20 Bead-Beater (Thetnica, Eslovenia, Europe). Sample was then centrifuge for 5 min at 14,000 g. The pellet containing the cell walls was washed five times with each of the following ice-cold solutions: distilled water, 5% NaCl, 2% NaCl, 1% NaCl and 1 mM PMSF. Then, cell walls were resuspended in sodium dodecyl sulphate (SDS) extraction buffer (50 mM tris-HCl, pH 8, 0.1 M EDTA, 2% (w/v) SDS and 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) and boiled at 100 °C for 10 min. Samples were centrifuged for 5 min at 14,000 g to recover the cell wall-associated proteins.  These proteins were precipitated by adding four volumes of 10% trichloroacetic acid and 0.07% 2-mercaptoethanol in acetone, and the obtained protein pellet was dissolved on rehydration buffer (7 M Urea, 2 M thiourea, %4 (w/v) CHAPS, 20 mM Tris). Then, they were separated by two-dimensional electrophoresis. For that 285 µg of protein were loaded into 7 cm long Immobiline DryStrip gels (pH 3-10, GE Healthcare) for the isoelectric focusing (IEF). The DryStrips were left to rehydrate overnight, then followed by isoelectric focusing at 500 V for 2000 Vhr, 1000 V for 3000 Vhr, 5000 V for 10 000 Vhr, and 5000 V for 40 000 Vhr; 50 μA per strip. Next, proteins were reduced 15 min equilibration buffer (6 M urea, 75 mM Tris-HCl pH 6.8, 25.5% [v/v] glycerol, 2% [w/v] SDS, 0.002% [w/v] bromophenol blue) with 1% (w/v) DTT and then alkylated for 15 min the same equilibration buffer with 2.5% (w/v) iodoacetamide. The strips were run in 10% acrylamide gels in the PROTEAN II xl Cell (Bio-Rad, Hercules, CA) at 70 mA per gel. The gels were stained with Coomassie Brilliant Blue, or transferred to a membrane to perform a Western Blot.  In the second case, proteins were transferred to Amersham Hybond-P PVDF membranes (GE Healthcare). First the membrane were immersed in methanol, distilled water, and transfer buffer (5,82 g/L tris-base, 2.93 g/L glycine and 200 ml methanol, pH 9.2) for 1 h at 400 mA. After immersing the membrane in methanol, distilled water and Tris buffered saline (TBS, Tris-HCl pH 7.5 amd 150 mM NaCl), it was blocked for 2 h with TBS Milk (TBSM, TBS supplemented with 5% (w/v) low fat dried milk and 0,1% (v/v) Tween 20). Then, it was washed 5 times with TBS for 5 minutes. Ca37 monoclonal antibody at 60 ug/mL was added and incubated O/N at 4 °C. After washing the membrane 5 times with TBS, 5 minutes each, anti-mouse IgG-HRP conjugated secondary antibody (DC02L, Merck) was added diluted 1:100,000 in TBSM and incubated for 30 minutes. The membrane was washed as before with TBS and the detection was visualized using the ECL Prime chemiluminiscence kit (NZYTech, Lisbon, Portugal) in a G:BOX Chemi imaging system (Syngene, Cambridge, United Kingdom). All incubation steps were performed at room temperature and agitation unless otherwise specified. The spots that were recognized by the monoclonal antibody were manually extracted from the gel stained with Coomassie Brilliant Blue G250. At the general services of research of the institution (SGIker), the gel extracts were swollen in digestion buffer (50 mM NH4HCO3, 12.5 ng/µL trypsin (Roche, Basel, Switzerland)) and incubated at 37 °C overnight. Then peptides were extracted, first with 25 mM NH4HCO3 and ACN, and second with 0.1% (v/v) trifluoroacetic acid and ACN. The recovered supernatants were pooled and dried in a SpeedVac (Thermo Electron, Waltham, MA, USA) and then dissolved in 10 µL of 0.1% (v/v) formic acid (FA) and sonicated for 5 min. The liquid chromatography was carried out on a EASY nLC-1200 (Thermo) (Waters, Milford, MA, USA) and the mass spectrophotometry in a Exploris 240 (Thermo). To do this, 8 µL from each sample was loaded into a Symmetry 300 C18, 180  µm × 20 mm precolumn (Waters) and washed with 0.1% (v/v) FA at a flow rate of 5 µL/min for 3 min. The precolumn was connected to a BEH130 C18, 75 µm × 200 mm, 1.7 µm (Waters), equilibrated in 3% (v/v) ACN and 0.1% (v/v) FA. Peptides were eluted with a 30 min linear gradient of 3–60% (v/v) ACN directly onto a NanoEase Emitter (Waters). Capillary voltage was set to 3500 V and data-dependent MS/MS acquisitions performed on precursors with charge states of 2, 3, or 4 over a survey m/z range of 350–1990. Reference: Pitarch, A., Sanchez, M., Nombela, C. and Gil, C., 2002. Sequential Fractionation and Two-dimensional Gel Analysis Unravels the Complexity of the Dimorphic Fungus Candida albicans Cell Wall Proteome. Mollecular & Cellular Proteomics. 1.12: 967-982

sampleProcessingProtocol: The endostyle tissues were isolated from S. clava adults, and subsequently shredded and homogenized. The homogenized tissues were incubated with RIPA lysis buffer, supplemented with 1% PMSF to effectively inhibit protease activity, for 20 mins on ice. Following this, high-speed centrifugation was carried out at 13201 × g for 5 mins at 4°C. The supernatant was then collected, and the protein concentration was determined using the Bicinchoninic Acid (BCA) Assay. Subsequently, the endostyle protein was incubated with the antibody specific to B. taurus TG protein (Supplementary Table 2) overnight at 4°C with shaking, to facilitate the formation of the antigen-antibody complex. Magnetic beads were then introduced into the system and incubated for 2 hours at room temperature, allowing the formation of the antigen-antibody-beads complex. Magnetic adsorption was subsequently performed using a magnetic rack to enrich the antigen-antibody-beads complex. After removing the supernatant, the complex was washed three times with PBS to ensure purity. Ultimately, the complex was collected for subsequent mass spectrometry identification. IgG was used as a negative control. The experiments were performed with two independent biological replicates. The obtained samples were sent to Shanghai Bioprofile Technology Company Ltd. for pretreatment, data acquisition, and analysis according to the following procedures. Gel pieces were cut from SDS PAGE, destained for 20 mins in 100 mM NH4HCO3 with 30% Acetonitrile and washed with Milli-Q water until the gels were destained. The spots were then lyophilized in a vacuum centrifuge. The in-gel proteins were reduced with dithiothreitol (10 mM DTT/ 100 mM NH4HCO3 ) for 30 mins at 56 °C, then alkylated with iodoacetamide (200 mM IAA/100 mM NH4HCO3) in the dark at room temperature for 30 mins. Gel pieces were briefly rinsed with 100 mM NH4HCO3 and ACN, respectively. Gel pieces were digested overnight in 12.5 ng/μl trypsin in 25 mM NH4HCO3. The peptides were extracted three times with 60% ACN/0.1% TFA. The extracts were pooled and dried completely by a vacuum centrifuge.
dataProcessingProtocol: LC-MS/MS The peptide of each sample was desalted on C18 Cartridges (Empore™ SPE Cartridges, Sigma), then concentrated by vacuum centrifugation and reconstituted in 10 µl of 0.1% (v/v) Formic acid. MS experiments were performed on a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer that was coupled to Easy nLC (Thermo Scientific). Peptide was first loaded onto a trap column (100μm×20mm, 5μm, C18) with 0.1% formic acid, then separated by an analytical column (75μm×100mm, 3μm, C18)) with a binary gradient of buffer A (0.1% Formic acid) and buffer B (84% acetonitrile and 0.1% Formic acid) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min over 60 mins. The gradient was set as following: 5%–8% buffer B from 0 min to 2mins, 8% to 23% buffer B from 2 mins to 42 mins, 23% to 40% buffer B from 42 mins to 50 mins, 40% to 100% buffer B from 50 mins to 52 mins, 100% buffer B kept till to 60mins. MS data was acquired using a data-dependent top20 method dynamically choosing the most abundant precursor ions from the survey scan (350–1800 m/z) for HCD fragmentation. A lock mass of 445.120025 Da was used as internal standard for mass calibration. The full MS scans were acquired at a resolution of 60,000 at m/z 200, and 15,000 at m/z 200 for MS/MS scan. The maximum injection time was set to for 50 ms for MS and 45 ms for MS/MS. Normalized collision energy was 27 and the isolation window was set to 1.5 Th. Dynamic exclusion duration was 30 s. Database search The MS data were analyzed using MaxQuant software version 1.5.8.3. MS data were searched against the database of S. clava genome. The trypsin was selected as digestion enzyme. The maximal two missed cleavage sites and the mass tolerance of 4.5 ppm for precursor ions and 20 ppm for fragment ions were defined for database search. Carbamidomethylation of cysteines was defined as fixed modification, while acetylation of protein N-terminal and Lysine, oxidation of Methionine, were set as variable modifications for database searching. The homogenized tissues were incubated with RIPA lysis buffer, supplemented with 1% PMSF to effectively inhibit protease activity, for 20 mins on ice. Following this, high-speed centrifugation was carried out at 13201 × g for 5 mins at 4°C. The supernatant was then collected, and the protein concentration was determined using the Bicinchoninic Acid (BCA) Assay. Subsequently, the endostyle protein was incubated with the antibody specific to B. taurus TG protein (Supplementary Table 2) overnight at 4°C with shaking, to facilitate the formation of the antigen-antibody complex. Magnetic beads were then introduced into the system and incubated for 2 hours at room temperature, allowing the formation of the antigen-antibody-beads complex. Magnetic adsorption was subsequently performed using a magnetic rack to enrich the antigen-antibody-beads complex. After removing the supernatant, the complex was washed three times with PBS to ensure purity. Ultimately, the complex was collected for subsequent mass spectrometry identification. IgG was used as a negative control. The experiments were performed with two independent biological replicates. The obtained samples were sent to Shanghai Bioprofile Technology Company Ltd. for pretreatment, data acquisition, and analysis according to the following procedures. Gel pieces were cut from SDS PAGE, destained for 20 mins in 100 mM NH4HCO3 with 30% Acetonitrile and washed with Milli-Q water until the gels were destained. The spots were then lyophilized in a vacuum centrifuge. The in-gel proteins were reduced with dithiothreitol (10 mM DTT/ 100 mM NH4HCO3 ) for 30 mins at 56 °C, then alkylated with iodoacetamide (200 mM IAA/100 mM NH4HCO3) in the dark at room temperature for 30 mins. Gel pieces were briefly rinsed with 100 mM NH4HCO3 and ACN, respectively. Gel pieces were digested overnight in 12.5 ng/μl trypsin in 25 mM NH4HCO3. The peptides were extracted three times with 60% ACN/0.1% TFA. The extracts were pooled and dried completely by a vacuum centrifuge. || LC-MS/MS The peptide of each sample was desalted on C18 Cartridges (Empore™ SPE Cartridges, Sigma), then concentrated by vacuum centrifugation and reconstituted in 10 µl of 0.1% (v/v) Formic acid. MS experiments were performed on a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer that was coupled to Easy nLC (Thermo Scientific). Peptide was first loaded onto a trap column (100μm×20mm, 5μm, C18) with 0.1% formic acid, then separated by an analytical column (75μm×100mm, 3μm, C18)) with a binary gradient of buffer A (0.1% Formic acid) and buffer B (84% acetonitrile and 0.1% Formic acid) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min over 60 mins. The gradient was set as following: 5%–8% buffer B from 0 min to 2mins, 8% to 23% buffer B from 2 mins to 42 mins, 23% to 40% buffer B from 42 mins to 50 mins, 40% to 100% buffer B from 50 mins to 52 mins, 100% buffer B kept till to 60mins. MS data was acquired using a data-dependent top20 method dynamically choosing the most abundant precursor ions from the survey scan (350–1800 m/z) for HCD fragmentation. A lock mass of 445.120025 Da was used as internal standard for mass calibration. The full MS scans were acquired at a resolution of 60,000 at m/z 200, and 15,000 at m/z 200 for MS/MS scan. The maximum injection time was set to for 50 ms for MS and 45 ms for MS/MS. Normalized collision energy was 27 and the isolation window was set to 1.5 Th. Dynamic exclusion duration was 30 s. Database search The MS data were analyzed using MaxQuant software version 1.5.8.3. MS data were searched against the database of S. clava genome. The trypsin was selected as digestion enzyme. The maximal two missed cleavage sites and the mass tolerance of 4.5 ppm for precursor ions and 20 ppm for fragment ions were defined for database search. Carbamidomethylation of cysteines was defined as fixed modification, while acetylation of protein N-terminal and Lysine, oxidation of Methionine, were set as variable modifications for database searching. The database search results were filtered and exported with <1% false discovery rate (FDR) at peptide level and protein level, respectively.
